title.en: Probability and maximum likelihood, from the definition
title.zh: 概率与最大似然：从定义出发

description.en: The rules of probability derived from one definition, Bayes' rule and its base-rate trap, the distributions of the subject, expectation, maximum likelihood by calculus, and entropy as expected surprise.
description.zh: 从一条定义推出全部概率规则，贝叶斯公式及其“基础概率”陷阱，这门课用到的分布，期望，用微积分求最大似然，以及把熵讲成“期望的惊讶”。

description.en: Ignoring the prior (base rate) when the evidence is imperfect
description.zh: 证据不完美时忽略先验（基础概率）
以为互斥事件就是独立事件

description.en: Reading a density value as a probability
Reading the likelihood of a parameter as the probability that the parameter is right
description.zh: 把参数的似然当成“参数正确的概率”

title.en: Why probability, and what you must write from memory
title.zh: 为什么要概率，以及哪些公式要默写

text.en: Look at the typical tasks: document $\to$ spam or not, handwritten digit $\to$ 0-9, purchase history $\to$ which book to recommend. In each, the honest answer is not 'it is spam' but 'it is spam with probability 0.9'. Probability is the language that lets a model say how sure it is, because data are few, noisy, or both.
text.zh: 看看典型任务：文档 $\to$ 是不是垃圾邮件，手写数字 $\to$ 0-9，购买记录 $\to$ 推荐哪本书。在每个任务里，诚实的回答不是“它是垃圾邮件”，而是“它有 0.9 的概率是垃圾邮件”。数据又少又吵（或两者兼有）的时候，概率就是让模型说出“有多确定”的语言。

items.en: **Uncertainty** from few observations and noisy data.
items.zh: **不确定性**：来自观测太少、数据有噪声。

items.en: **Features follow distributions**: we model how a class generates its attribute values.
items.zh: **特征服从分布**：我们为“一个类别怎样产生属性值”建模。

items.en: **Soft predictions**: 'we are 60% confident Bob will like this book'.
items.zh: **软预测**：“我们有 60% 的把握 Bob 会喜欢这本书”。

text.en: A probabilistic model formalises a hypothesis as a distribution and uses the laws of probability to derive predictions (George Box: all models are wrong, some are useful). This lesson is the toolbox: the laws, the distributions, how to fit a distribution to data (maximum likelihood), and entropy, which leads straight into decision trees.
text.zh: 概率模型把假设形式化为分布，再用概率定律推出预测（George Box：所有模型都是错的，但有些有用）。这一课就是工具箱：定律、分布、怎样让分布去拟合数据（最大似然），以及通向决策树的熵。

title.en: The exam gives you no probability formulas

body.en: Lecture 23: formulas are printed next to each question **except probability**. So this lesson derives each rule from the one before, because a rule you can derive is a rule you can reproduce. A recall page near the end lists what to write from memory.
body.zh: 第 23 讲：每道题旁边都会印公式，**唯独概率除外**。所以这一课把每条规则都从前一条推出来，能推出来的规则就能默写出来。接近结尾有一页默写清单。

title.zh: 事件、联合概率与条件概率

text.en: $P(A=a)$ is the probability that the random variable $A$ takes the value $a$: the fraction of times the event is true over many independent trials. It lies in $[0,1]$, a certain event has probability 1, an impossible one 0, and over a set of mutually exclusive, exhaustive outcomes the probabilities sum to 1. We often write $P(x)$ for $P(A=x)$, and $P(A)$ for the whole distribution over $A$ (a histogram).
text.zh: $P(A=a)$ 是随机变量 $A$ 取值 $a$ 的概率：很多次独立试验中该事件为真的比例。它落在 $[0,1]$ 内，必然事件为 1，不可能事件为 0，一组互斥且穷尽的结果，概率之和为 1。常把 $P(A=x)$ 简写成 $P(x)$，而 $P(A)$ 表示 $A$ 的整个分布（一张直方图）。

text.en: The deck's world is a deck of 52 cards: 13 ranks in 4 suits, hearts and diamonds red, clubs and spades black.
text.zh: 讲义的世界是一副 52 张的牌：4 种花色、各 13 个点数，红桃和方块是红色，梅花和黑桃是黑色。

rows.en: disjoint: no card is both, so add
rows.zh: 互斥：没有牌既是 A 又是 K，所以相加

text.en: For disjoint events $P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B)$. If they can overlap, the overlap is counted twice and must be taken off once: $P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A, B)$ (ace or heart: $4/52 + 13/52 - 1/52 = 16/52$).
text.zh: 互斥事件满足 $P(A \text{ 或 } B) = P(A) + P(B)$。若两者可能重叠，重叠部分被数了两次，要减掉一次：$P(A \text{ 或 } B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A, B)$（A 或红桃：$4/52 + 13/52 - 1/52 = 16/52$）。

text.en: Joint and conditional
text.zh: 联合与条件

text.en: The **joint** probability $P(A,B) = P(A \cap B)$ is the probability that both happen: $P(\text{ace}, \text{spade}) = 1/52$, $P(\text{heart}, \text{red}) = 13/52$. The **conditional** probability asks the question inside a smaller world: *given that $B$ is true, how likely is $A$?*
text.zh: **联合**概率 $P(A,B) = P(A \cap B)$ 是两件事都发生的概率：$P(\text{A}, \text{黑桃}) = 1/52$，$P(\text{红桃}, \text{红色}) = 13/52$。**条件**概率是在一个更小的世界里发问：*已知 $B$ 为真，$A$ 有多大可能？*

text.en: Read it as two steps. Throw away every outcome where $B$ is false (the denominator $P(B)$ is the size of the world that remains). Of that world, count the part where $A$ is also true (the numerator). In the picture: of the 26 red cards, 13 are hearts.
text.zh: 分两步读。把 $B$ 为假的结果全部扔掉（分母 $P(B)$ 就是剩下的世界的大小）。在这个世界里，数 $A$ 也为真的那一部分（分子）。看图：26 张红牌里，13 张是红桃。

alt.en: A 13 by 4 grid of the 52 cards. The two red rows are outlined (26 cards), the hearts row inside them is the darker row (13 cards). P(heart | red) = 13/26, P(heart, red) = 13/52.
alt.zh: 52 张牌排成 13 乘 4 的格子。两个红色行（26 张）用框标出，其中的红桃行颜色更深（13 张）。P(红桃 | 红色) = 13/26，P(红桃, 红色) = 13/52。

text.en: The conditional is **not symmetric**: $P(\text{heart} \mid \text{red}) = 13/26 = 1/2$, but $P(\text{red} \mid \text{heart}) = 13/13 = 1$. Confusing the two is the most common mistake in this topic.
text.zh: 条件概率**不对称**：$P(\text{红桃} \mid \text{红色}) = 13/26 = 1/2$，但 $P(\text{红色} \mid \text{红桃}) = 13/13 = 1$。把两者弄混是这个话题里最常见的错误。

feedback.en: That is the joint $P(\text{ace}, \text{spade})$. For the conditional, restrict to the 13 spades first.
feedback.zh: 那是联合概率 $P(\text{A}, \text{黑桃})$。条件概率要先把范围限制到 13 张黑桃。

feedback.en: That is $P(\text{ace})$ in the whole deck, ignoring the information that the card is a spade.
feedback.zh: 那是整副牌里的 $P(\text{A})$，没用上“这张牌是黑桃”这条信息。

explain.en: $P(\text{ace} \mid \text{spade}) = \frac{1/52}{13/52} = \frac{1}{13}$. It equals $P(\text{ace})$ too: knowing the suit tells you nothing about the rank. That is independence, next.
explain.zh: $P(\text{A} \mid \text{黑桃}) = \frac{1/52}{13/52} = \frac{1}{13}$。它也等于 $P(\text{A})$：知道花色并不告诉你点数。这就是独立性，下一页讲。

text.en: $A$ and $B$ are **independent** exactly when the joint is the product of the parts:
text.zh: $A$ 与 $B$ **独立**，当且仅当联合概率等于各自概率的乘积：

blocks.tex: P(A, B) = P(A)\,P(B) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad P(A \mid B) = P(A)

text.en: The second form says what it means: learning $B$ does not change your belief about $A$ (divide the first form by $P(B)$ to see they are the same). The deck's two cases:
text.zh: 第二种写法说出了它的含义：知道 $B$ 并不改变你对 $A$ 的信念（把第一种写法两边除以 $P(B)$ 就得到第二种）。讲义的两个例子：

rows.en: dependent: red makes heart twice as likely
rows.zh: 不独立：红色让红桃的可能性翻倍

body.en: If $A$ and $B$ are disjoint and both possible, then $P(A,B) = 0 \ne P(A)P(B)$. They are as dependent as can be: if one happens the other cannot.
body.zh: 若 $A$ 与 $B$ 互斥且都有可能发生，则 $P(A,B) = 0 \ne P(A)P(B)$。它们依赖得不能再依赖了：一个发生，另一个就不可能发生。

text.en: Conditional independence
text.zh: 条件独立

text.en: $A$ and $B$ are **conditionally independent given $C$** if, once $C$ is known, $B$ tells nothing more about $A$:
text.zh: 如果已知 $C$ 之后，$B$ 不再提供关于 $A$ 的任何信息，就说 $A$ 与 $B$ **在给定 $C$ 时条件独立**：

blocks.tex: P(A, B \mid C) = P(A \mid C)\,P(B \mid C) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad P(A \mid B, C) = P(A \mid C)

text.en: The two notions are separate: neither implies the other. Example: it is hot with probability 0.5. On a hot day, ice cream is bought ($A$) with probability 0.8, sunburn ($B$) occurs with probability 0.6; on a cold day 0.2 and 0.1. Given the temperature, the two are independent by construction.
text.zh: 这是两个独立的概念：谁也推不出谁。例子：天热的概率为 0.5。热天买冰淇淋（$A$）的概率为 0.8，晒伤（$B$）的概率为 0.6；冷天分别为 0.2 和 0.1。给定温度，两者按构造独立。

text.en: But without the temperature: $P(A) = 0.5$, $P(B) = 0.35$, $P(A,B) = 0.5(0.8)(0.6) + 0.5(0.2)(0.1) = 0.25$, while $P(A)P(B) = 0.175$. Ice cream and sunburn are dependent, because heat drives both; conditioning on the heat removes the link.
text.zh: 但不看温度：$P(A) = 0.5$，$P(B) = 0.35$，$P(A,B) = 0.5(0.8)(0.6) + 0.5(0.2)(0.1) = 0.25$，而 $P(A)P(B) = 0.175$。冰淇淋和晒伤是相关的，因为天热同时推动了两者；给定温度就切断了这条联系。

text.en: Remember this shape: **a common cause makes effects dependent; conditioning on the cause makes them independent again.** Naive Bayes assumes exactly this, that the attributes are independent given the class.
text.zh: 记住这个形状：**共同的原因使结果相关；给定原因后它们又独立了。**朴素贝叶斯假设的正是这个：给定类别后，各属性相互独立。

label.en: Conditional independence given $C$ does not imply plain independence (the temperature example)
label.zh: 给定 $C$ 的条件独立并不意味着无条件独立（温度的例子）

label.en: If $A$ and $B$ are independent they are independent given any $C$
label.zh: 如果 $A$ 与 $B$ 独立，则对任何 $C$ 它们都条件独立

feedback.en: Not in general: two fair coins are independent, but given $C$ = "the two coins agree" they are completely dependent.
feedback.zh: 一般不成立：两枚公平硬币相互独立，但给定 $C$ =“两枚硬币结果相同”，它们就完全相关了。

label.en: Disjoint events with positive probability are independent
label.zh: 概率为正的互斥事件是独立的

feedback.en: Disjoint means $P(A,B)=0$, but $P(A)P(B)>0$. They are dependent.
feedback.zh: 互斥意味着 $P(A,B)=0$，而 $P(A)P(B)>0$。它们是相关的。

explain.en: Independence and conditional independence are different properties; either can hold without the other.
explain.zh: 独立与条件独立是不同的性质，一个成立时另一个不一定成立。

title.zh: 边缘化：把一个变量求和消掉

text.en: Sometimes you hold a joint table and want the probability of $A$ alone, whatever $B$ is. Every outcome of $A$ happens together with exactly one outcome of $B$, so add up over all of them:
text.zh: 有时你手里是一张联合分布表，想知道的只是 $A$ 本身的概率，不管 $B$ 是什么。$A$ 的每个结果都恰好和 $B$ 的一个结果同时发生，所以把它们全加起来：

text.en: The deck's example: the probability that a movie succeeds, by genre $A$ and market $B$. The margins of the table are the sums of its rows and columns (hence the name).
text.zh: 讲义的例子：一部电影成功的概率，按类型 $A$ 和市场 $B$ 划分。表的边缘就是各行各列的和（“边缘”由此得名）。

text.en: Summing a row gives the genre: romance $0.05+0.1+0.3 = 0.45$. Summing a column gives the market: AUS $0.3+0.1+0.025 = 0.425$. Both margins add to 1. Conditionals come out of the same table: $P(\text{romance} \mid \text{AUS}) = 0.3/0.425 = 0.706$, while $P(\text{AUS} \mid \text{romance}) = 0.3/0.45 = 0.667$: a different number, as the asymmetry says.
text.zh: 一行加起来是类型：浪漫片 $0.05+0.1+0.3 = 0.45$。一列加起来是市场：AUS $0.3+0.1+0.025 = 0.425$。两条边缘之和都是 1。条件概率也出自这张表：$P(\text{浪漫} \mid \text{AUS}) = 0.3/0.425 = 0.706$，而 $P(\text{AUS} \mid \text{浪漫}) = 0.3/0.45 = 0.667$：数字不同，这正是不对称性。

text.en: Combine marginalisation with the product rule (next page) and you get the **law of total probability**, the denominator of Bayes' rule: $P(A) = \sum_b P(A \mid b)\,P(b)$.
text.zh: 把边缘化和乘法规则（下一页）合起来，就得到**全概率公式**，也就是贝叶斯公式的分母：$P(A) = \sum_b P(A \mid b)\,P(b)$。

feedback.en: That is one cell, thriller in NA. Sum the whole NA column.
feedback.zh: 那只是一个格子（NA 的惊悚片）。要把整个 NA 列加起来。

feedback.en: That is the thriller row total $P(\text{thriller})$, not the NA column.
feedback.zh: 那是惊悚片这一行的合计 $P(\text{惊悚})$，不是 NA 这一列。

explain.en: Column sums are the market probabilities: 0.25, 0.325, 0.425.

title.en: Product rule and chain rule, from the definition
title.zh: 乘法规则与链式法则：从定义推出

say.en: The definition of the conditional probability: the share of the world where $B$ holds in which $A$ holds too.
say.zh: 条件概率的定义：在 $B$ 成立的世界里，$A$ 也成立的那一份。

say.en: Multiply both sides by $P(B)$. This is the **product rule**: to have both, first have $B$, then $A$ within it.
say.zh: 两边乘以 $P(B)$。这就是**乘法规则**：要两者都发生，先有 $B$，再在其中有 $A$。

say.en: Swap the roles. $P(A,B)$ and $P(B,A)$ are the same event, so the same joint can be built in either order.
say.zh: 把角色对调。$P(A,B)$ 与 $P(B,A)$ 是同一个事件，所以同一个联合概率可以按任一顺序搭起来。

say.en: Apply the product rule twice: treat $(A_1, A_2)$ as one event, then split it.
say.zh: 用两次乘法规则：把 $(A_1, A_2)$ 看作一个事件，再把它拆开。

say.en: Continue: this is the **chain rule**. Each factor conditions on everything before it. It makes no assumption: it is always true.
say.zh: 一直这样做下去，就是**链式法则**。每个因子都以它之前的全部为条件。它不含任何假设，永远成立。

say.en: The deck's example: two kings in a row without replacement. After one king is gone, 3 kings remain among 51 cards.
say.zh: 讲义的例子：不放回地连抽两张 K。抽走一张 K 后，51 张牌里剩 3 张 K。

lines.tex: P(M, T, S) = P(T)\,P(S \mid T)\,P(M \mid T, S)

say.en: The deck's example with $M$ = July, $T$ = 5 degrees, $S$ = sick. The order is free: any ordering of the variables gives a correct factorisation. Some are more natural (July causes 5 degrees causes sickness) and easier to estimate, but all are equal.
say.zh: 顺序是自由的：变量的任何排列都给出正确的分解。有些更自然（七月导致 5 度导致生病），也更容易估计，但它们全都相等。

outro.en: Keep the picture: a joint probability is a product of conditionals. Naive Bayes will simplify each factor with an independence assumption.
outro.zh: 记住这个图景：联合概率是若干条件概率的乘积。朴素贝叶斯会用独立性假设来化简每一个因子。

prompt.en: Probability of drawing two kings in a row without replacement (give a fraction).
prompt.zh: 不放回连抽两张 K 的概率（写成分数）。

say.en: Both sides equal the joint $P(A,B)$ by the product rule, one in each order.
say.zh: 由乘法规则，两边都等于联合概率 $P(A,B)$，只是顺序不同。

say.en: Divide by $P(B)$. This is **Bayes' rule**: it turns a conditional around.
say.zh: 除以 $P(B)$。这就是**贝叶斯公式**：把条件概率“翻个面”。

say.en: The four names. $A$ is the hypothesis, $B$ the evidence. ① Posterior: belief in $A$ after the evidence. ② Likelihood: how probable the evidence is if $A$ is true. ③ Prior: belief in $A$ before the evidence. ④ Evidence: how common $B$ is overall.
say.zh: 四个名字。$A$ 是假设，$B$ 是证据。① 后验：看到证据后对 $A$ 的信念。② 似然：若 $A$ 为真，证据有多可能。③ 先验：看到证据前对 $A$ 的信念。④ 证据项：$B$ 总体上有多常见。

say.en: The denominator is not a new quantity: marginalise the joint over all hypotheses, then use the product rule on each term.
say.zh: 分母不是新量：把联合概率对所有假设边缘化，再对每一项用乘法规则。

say.en: The full form, with a sum over the hypotheses $a'$ in the denominator. It is what you use when the evidence $P(B)$ is not given.
say.zh: 完整形式，分母对各个假设 $a'$ 求和。证据 $P(B)$ 没给出时就用它。

say.en: The denominator is the same for every $a$, so it only rescales until the posteriors sum to 1. To compare hypotheses, compare likelihood times prior.
say.zh: 分母对每个 $a$ 都一样，它只是把后验缩放到总和为 1。比较各个假设，只要比较似然乘先验。

intro.en: Everything needed is on the previous page: the definition of the conditional, the product rule, and marginalisation.
intro.zh: 需要的东西上一页都有了：条件概率的定义、乘法规则和边缘化。

outro.en: Why this matters for learning: $P(B \mid A)$ ('how does the class produce these features?') is easy to estimate from data; $P(A \mid B)$ ('which class, given these features?') is what we want. Bayes' rule is the bridge, and it is the heart of naive Bayes.
outro.zh: 它对学习的意义：$P(B \mid A)$（“这个类别怎样产生这些特征？”）容易从数据里估计；$P(A \mid B)$（“看到这些特征，是哪个类别？”）才是我们想要的。贝叶斯公式就是桥梁，也是朴素贝叶斯的核心。

title.en: Bayes' rule at work, and the base-rate trap
title.zh: 贝叶斯公式用起来：基础概率陷阱

text.en: The deck's example. Estimate the probability that a student studied hard ($S$) given that they got an H1 ($H$). Known: $P(S) = 0.3$ (prior rate of hard-working students), $P(H \mid S) = 0.6$, $P(H) = 0.2$ (measured).
text.zh: 讲义的例子。已知一个学生拿了 H1（$H$），估计他努力学习（$S$）的概率。已知：$P(S) = 0.3$（努力学生的先验比例），$P(H \mid S) = 0.6$，$P(H) = 0.2$（实测）。

text.en: The deck asks: what if $P(H) = 0.4$? Then $0.3 \times 0.6 / 0.4 = 0.45$. A larger denominator means H1s are common anyway, so an H1 is weaker evidence of hard work. Sanity check the inputs: $P(H) \ge P(H, S) = 0.3 \times 0.6 = 0.18$, so $0.2$ is possible but only just; $P(H)=0.15$ would be impossible and would give a posterior above 1.
text.zh: 讲义追问：如果 $P(H) = 0.4$ 呢？则 $0.3 \times 0.6 / 0.4 = 0.45$。分母越大，说明 H1 本来就常见，所以 H1 对“努力学习”的证明力就越弱。顺手检查输入：$P(H) \ge P(H, S) = 0.3 \times 0.6 = 0.18$，所以 $0.2$ 是可能的，但已很勉强；$P(H)=0.15$ 就不可能了，算出的后验会超过 1。

text.en: The classic trap is **base-rate neglect**: answering with the likelihood and forgetting the prior. The posterior needs both. A test that is right 90% of the time, for a condition that 2% of people have, still mostly flags healthy people, because healthy people are 49 times more common. The taxi problem on the next page makes this exact.
text.zh: 经典陷阱是**忽视基础概率**：只用似然回答，忘了先验。后验两者都需要。一个 90% 准确的检测，针对只有 2% 的人患有的病，标出来的仍然多数是健康人，因为健康人多 49 倍。下一页的出租车问题把这一点算清楚。

prompt.en: A cause is rare (prior 1%) but a test for it has likelihood $P(\text{positive} \mid \text{cause}) = 0.99$. Which statement holds?
prompt.zh: 某病因很少见（先验 1%），但检测的似然 $P(\text{阳性} \mid \text{病因}) = 0.99$。哪个说法成立？

label.en: The posterior can be small: it depends on the prior and on how often the test is positive without the cause
label.zh: 后验可能很小：取决于先验，以及没有病因时检测也呈阳性的频率

label.en: The posterior is 0.99, since the test is accurate

feedback.en: That is the likelihood, $P(\text{positive} \mid \text{cause})$, not the posterior $P(\text{cause} \mid \text{positive})$.
feedback.zh: 那是似然 $P(\text{阳性} \mid \text{病因})$，不是后验 $P(\text{病因} \mid \text{阳性})$。

feedback.en: The prior is only where you start. A positive result raises it, by how much depends on the evidence.
feedback.zh: 先验只是起点。阳性结果会把它抬高，抬多少取决于证据。

explain.en: Posterior $\propto$ likelihood $\times$ prior: a tiny prior can cancel a strong likelihood.
explain.zh: 后验 $\propto$ 似然 $\times$ 先验：很小的先验可以抵消很强的似然。

say.en: Start with a concrete city of 1000 cabs: 15% are red (150) and 85% orange (850). Counting people is easier than multiplying probabilities.
say.zh: 想象一座有 1000 辆出租车的城市：15% 红色（150 辆）、85% 橙色（850 辆）。数“多少辆”比乘概率容易。

say.en: The witness is wrong 20% of the time, so right 80%. Of the 150 red cabs, 120 are correctly called red.
say.zh: 目击者 20% 的时候会错，所以 80% 对。150 辆红车里，120 辆被正确地说成红色。

say.en: Of the 850 orange cabs, 170 are wrongly called red.
say.zh: 850 辆橙车里，170 辆被错说成红色。

say.en: The witness says 'red' for 290 cabs in all. This is the evidence $P(R=\text{red})$ times 1000.
say.zh: 目击者一共对 290 辆车说“红色”。这就是证据项 $P(R=\text{红})$ 乘以 1000。

say.en: Here $C$ is the true colour, $R$ the reported one, $r$ = red. Among the cabs called red, 120 really are red. Most people answer 80%: they use the likelihood and ignore that red cabs are rare.
say.zh: 这里 $C$ 是真实颜色，$R$ 是报告的颜色，$r$ 表示红。在被说成红色的车里，真的是红色的有 120 辆。多数人回答 80%：他们只用了似然，忽略了红车本来就少。

say.en: The same in Bayes' rule with the evidence expanded by marginalisation. The numerator is the red-and-called-red mass, the denominator adds orange-and-called-red.
say.zh: 同样的事用贝叶斯公式写：证据项用边缘化展开。分子是“红色且被说成红”的份额，分母再加上“橙色且被说成红”。

intro.en: Taxi-cab problem (Tversky and Kahneman, 1972): 85% of cabs are orange, 15% red. An eyewitness says the cab in an accident was red, and is wrong 20% of the time. What is the probability it was red?
intro.zh: 出租车问题（Tversky 和 Kahneman，1972）：85% 的出租车是橙色，15% 是红色。目击者说肇事车是红色，他有 20% 的时候会说错。这辆车真是红色的概率是多少？

outro.en: **Answer:** $0.12/0.29 = 0.414$, about 41%. The report moves the belief from 15% to 41%, a lot, but not to 80%.

prompt.en: How many of the 1000 cabs does the witness call red?
prompt.zh: 1000 辆车里，目击者会把几辆说成红色？

title.en: Random variables, distributions and the Gaussian
title.zh: 随机变量、分布与高斯分布

text.en: A **random variable** is a variable whose value is the outcome of a random phenomenon, and its **distribution** says how likely each outcome is. A **discrete** variable takes countably many values (heads in coin flips, the card rank); a **continuous** one takes values on a continuum (the height of a student).
text.zh: **随机变量**是取值由随机现象的结果决定的变量，它的**分布**说明每个结果有多可能。**离散**变量取可数个值（抛硬币的正面数、牌的点数）；**连续**变量在连续区间里取值（学生的身高）。

text.en: For a discrete variable the distribution is a table of probabilities that sum to 1. For a continuous one there are infinitely many values, each with probability 0, so we use a **density** $p(x)$: probabilities are *areas* under it, $P(a \le X \le b) = \int_a^b p(x)\,dx$, and the total area is 1.
text.zh: 离散变量的分布是一张总和为 1 的概率表。连续变量有无穷多个取值，每个值的概率都是 0，所以用**密度** $p(x)$：概率是密度曲线下的*面积*，$P(a \le X \le b) = \int_a^b p(x)\,dx$，总面积为 1。

title.en: A density value is not a probability

body.en: A density can exceed 1: a Gaussian with $\sigma = 0.1$ has peak height about 3.99, yet it is still a valid distribution because its area is 1. Only areas are probabilities.
body.zh: 密度可以大于 1：$\sigma = 0.1$ 的高斯分布峰值约 3.99，但它仍是合法的分布，因为面积是 1。只有面积才是概率。

text.en: The **Gaussian (normal)** distribution is the continuous, symmetric, bell-shaped one, with two parameters: the mean $\mu$ (the most typical value, the centre) and the standard deviation $\sigma$ (the spread; $\sigma^2$ is the variance).
text.zh: **高斯（正态）分布**是连续、对称、钟形的分布，有两个参数：均值 $\mu$（最典型的值，中心）和标准差 $\sigma$（离散程度；$\sigma^2$ 是方差）。

items.en: $(x-\mu)^2/\sigma^2$: the squared distance from the centre, measured in units of $\sigma$. The minus sign makes the height fall as $x$ moves away.
items.zh: $(x-\mu)^2/\sigma^2$：到中心的距离的平方，以 $\sigma$ 为单位。负号让 $x$ 离中心越远，高度越低。

items.en: $\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}$: the constant that makes the total area exactly 1. A wider curve (larger $\sigma$) must be lower.
items.zh: $\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}$：让总面积恰为 1 的常数。曲线越宽（$\sigma$ 越大）就必须越矮。

items.en: Rule of thumb: about 68% of the area lies within $\mu \pm \sigma$, 95% within $\mu \pm 2\sigma$.
items.zh: 经验法则：约 68% 的面积在 $\mu \pm \sigma$ 之内，95% 在 $\mu \pm 2\sigma$ 之内。

alt.en: Three Gaussian curves: mu 0 sigma 1 (blue), mu 0 sigma 2 (orange, wider and lower), mu 3 sigma 1 (green, shifted right).
alt.zh: 三条高斯曲线：μ=0、σ=1（蓝）；μ=0、σ=2（橙，更宽更矮）；μ=3、σ=1（绿，右移）。

prompt.en: Keeping $\mu$, you double $\sigma$. What happens to the peak height of the density?
prompt.zh: 保持 $\mu$ 不变，把 $\sigma$ 加倍。密度的峰值高度怎样变？

feedback.en: The prefactor is $1/(\sigma\sqrt{2\pi})$, with $\sigma$ in the denominator: a wider curve is lower, since the area must stay 1.
feedback.zh: 前面的系数是 $1/(\sigma\sqrt{2\pi})$，$\sigma$ 在分母里：曲线变宽就变矮，因为面积必须保持 1。

label.en: It stays the same; only the tails change

feedback.en: At $x=\mu$ the exponent is 0, so the height is exactly the prefactor, which changes with $\sigma$.
feedback.zh: $x=\mu$ 时指数为 0，高度恰好是前面的系数，它随 $\sigma$ 变化。

explain.en: Peak height is $1/(\sigma\sqrt{2\pi})$: halved when $\sigma$ doubles.
explain.zh: 峰值高度是 $1/(\sigma\sqrt{2\pi})$：$\sigma$ 加倍则减半。

title.zh: 伯努利、二项、类别、多项分布

text.en: Four discrete distributions form a small table. Rows: one trial or many. Columns: two outcomes or more.
text.zh: 四个离散分布组成一张小表。行：一次试验还是多次。列：两个结果还是更多。

text.en: Bernoulli: one coin
text.zh: 伯努利：一枚硬币

text.en: Just a compact way to write two cases: $x=1$ gives $p^1(1-p)^0 = p$ (success), $x=0$ gives $p^0(1-p)^1 = 1-p$ (failure). The exponents switch the unwanted factor off.
text.zh: 只是把两种情形写成一个式子：$x=1$ 得 $p^1(1-p)^0 = p$（成功），$x=0$ 得 $p^0(1-p)^1 = 1-p$（失败）。指数把不需要的那个因子“关掉”。

text.en: Binomial: the number of successes in $N$ independent Bernoulli trials
text.zh: 二项：$N$ 次独立伯努利试验里的成功次数

items.en: $p^{x}(1-p)^{N-x}$: the probability of **one particular sequence** with $x$ successes (trials multiply because they are independent).
items.zh: $p^{x}(1-p)^{N-x}$：某**一个特定序列**（恰有 $x$ 次成功）的概率（试验独立，所以相乘）。

items.en: $\frac{N!}{x!(N-x)!} = \binom{N}{x}$: the **number of sequences** that have $x$ successes. Each has the same probability, so multiply.
items.zh: $\frac{N!}{x!(N-x)!} = \binom{N}{x}$：有 $x$ 次成功的**序列个数**。每个序列概率相同，所以相乘。

text.en: Categorical and multinomial: a die instead of a coin
text.zh: 类别与多项：用骰子代替硬币

text.en: A single roll of a $K$-sided die is **categorical** with probabilities $p_1,\dots,p_K$ (summing to 1): $P(X=k) = p_k$. Repeat $N$ times and count how often each face came up, $x_1,\dots,x_K$ (with $\sum_k x_k = N$): the counts are **multinomial**.
text.zh: 掷一次 $K$ 面骰子是**类别分布**，各面概率 $p_1,\dots,p_K$（和为 1）：$P(X=k) = p_k$。重复 $N$ 次，数每个面出现了几次 $x_1,\dots,x_K$（$\sum_k x_k = N$）：这些计数服从**多项分布**。

text.en: Same structure as the binomial: the product $\prod p_k^{x_k}$ is the probability of one particular sequence with those counts, and the fraction counts the sequences. (The deck writes the categorical as that bare product; it is the probability of one specific sequence, without the counting factor.) Special cases: $K=2$ gives the binomial, $N=1$ gives the categorical, $N=1, K=2$ the Bernoulli. The multinomial is the workhorse of text models: word counts in a document.
text.zh: 结构和二项一样：乘积 $\prod p_k^{x_k}$ 是具有这些计数的某一个特定序列的概率，分式数的是序列的个数。（讲义把类别分布写成那个裸乘积；它是一个特定序列的概率，没有计数因子。）特例：$K=2$ 是二项，$N=1$ 是类别，$N=1, K=2$ 是伯努利。多项分布是文本模型的主力：一篇文档里的词频。

say.en: The deck's coin: 2 heads in 3 tosses of a fair coin. First the probability of one particular sequence, say HHT. Tosses are independent, so multiply.
say.zh: 讲义的硬币例子：公平硬币抛 3 次，恰好 2 次正面。先算某一个特定序列（比如 HHT）的概率。各次独立，所以相乘。

say.en: How many sequences have 2 heads? HHT, HTH, THH: three. The formula chooses which 2 of the 3 positions hold the heads.
say.zh: 有几个序列恰有 2 次正面？HHT、HTH、THH：三个。公式是在 3 个位置里选出哪 2 个放正面。

say.en: Each of the three sequences has probability 1/8; add them (they are disjoint events).
say.zh: 三个序列各有 1/8 的概率；把它们加起来（它们是互斥事件）。

say.en: Now the deck's die: roll a fair die 5 times; probability of exactly 3 ones and 2 fives. One particular sequence, e.g. 1,1,1,5,5: every roll has probability 1/6, five rolls.
say.zh: 再看讲义的骰子：公平骰子掷 5 次，恰好 3 个一点和 2 个五点。某一个特定序列（如 1,1,1,5,5）：每次掷出的概率都是 1/6，共 5 次。

say.en: The number of orderings of three 1s and two 5s. The four faces that never appear contribute $0! = 1$.
say.zh: 三个 1 和两个 5 有多少种排法。四个从未出现的面各贡献 $0! = 1$。

say.en: Orderings times the probability of one sequence.
say.zh: 排法数乘以单个序列的概率。

outro.en: Both answers have the same shape: (number of arrangements) $\times$ (probability of one arrangement).
outro.zh: 两个答案是同一个形状：（排列数）$\times$（单个排列的概率）。

prompt.en: Probability of exactly 2 heads in 3 fair tosses (a fraction).
prompt.zh: 公平硬币抛 3 次恰好 2 次正面的概率（分数）。

say.en: The **expectation** is the average of the values, each weighted by its probability: the long-run mean over many repetitions.
say.zh: **期望**是各个取值按概率加权的平均：重复很多次后的长期均值。

say.en: A fair die $D$. Note that the expectation need not be a value the variable can take.
say.zh: 公平骰子 $D$。注意期望不必是变量能取到的值。

say.en: A Bernoulli variable $B$ is 1 with probability $p$, else 0.
say.zh: 伯努利变量 $B$ 以概率 $p$ 取 1，否则取 0。

say.en: **Linearity**: the expectation of a sum is the sum of expectations. It needs no independence.
say.zh: **线性性**：和的期望等于期望之和。不需要独立。

say.en: A binomial count $X$ is a sum of $N$ Bernoulli variables, so its expectation is $N$ times $p$. For the deck's spam model, $N=100$ and $\theta=0.2$ give 20 spam emails expected in an inbox.
say.zh: 二项计数 $X$ 是 $N$ 个伯努利变量之和，所以期望是 $N$ 乘 $p$。讲义的垃圾邮件模型里，$N=100$、$\theta=0.2$，一个收件箱预期有 20 封垃圾邮件。

say.en: The expectation of a function of $X$: weight $f(x)$, not $x$. This is how an **expected loss** (the generalisation error) and, below, entropy are defined.
say.zh: $X$ 的函数的期望：加权的是 $f(x)$ 而不是 $x$。**期望损失**（泛化误差）和后面的熵都是这样定义的。

say.en: The **variance** is the expected squared distance from the mean $\mu$; expanding the square gives the second form. For a Bernoulli, $\mathbb{E}[X^2] = p$, so $\mathrm{Var} = p - p^2 = p(1-p)$; independent trials add, so a binomial has $Np(1-p)$ (16 for the spam model).
say.zh: **方差**是到均值 $\mu$ 的距离平方的期望；把平方展开得到第二种写法。伯努利有 $\mathbb{E}[X^2] = p$，所以 $\mathrm{Var} = p - p^2 = p(1-p)$；独立试验的方差相加，所以二项是 $Np(1-p)$（垃圾邮件模型里是 16）。

outro.en: For the Gaussian, $\mathbb{E}[X] = \mu$ and $\mathrm{Var}[X] = \sigma^2$, which is why those are its parameters.
outro.zh: 高斯分布有 $\mathbb{E}[X] = \mu$、$\mathrm{Var}[X] = \sigma^2$，这就是它的参数叫这两个名字的原因。

text.en: The deck's model: an email is spam with probability $\theta$. The number of spam emails in an inbox of $N=100$ is $X \sim \text{Binomial}(N=100, \theta)$. To predict anything we need $\theta$, but it is unknown. What we have is data: an inbox with $x$ spam emails.
text.zh: 讲义的模型：一封邮件是垃圾邮件的概率为 $\theta$。$N=100$ 封邮件的收件箱里的垃圾邮件数是 $X \sim \text{Binomial}(N=100, \theta)$。要预测任何东西都需要 $\theta$，但它未知。我们手里有的是数据：一个收件箱里有 $x$ 封垃圾邮件。

text.en: Turn the question around. The probability $P(X=x;N,\theta)$ has two inputs, the data $x$ and the parameter $\theta$. Probability fixes $\theta$ and asks about the data. The **likelihood** fixes the data and asks how well each $\theta$ explains them:
text.zh: 把问题倒过来。概率 $P(X=x;N,\theta)$ 有两个输入：数据 $x$ 和参数 $\theta$。“概率”固定 $\theta$、问数据；**似然**固定数据、问每个 $\theta$ 对数据解释得有多好：

text.en: The **maximum likelihood estimate (MLE)** is the $\theta$ under which the observed data were most probable. Take 7 spam emails in 10: with $\theta = 0.7$, $L = \binom{10}{7}\,0.7^{7}\,0.3^{3} = 0.267$; with $\theta = 0.5$, only $0.117$. The curve of $L$ against $\theta$ peaks at $0.7$, and with ten times the data it peaks at the same place but much more sharply: more data, more certainty.
text.zh: **最大似然估计（MLE）**是使观测数据最可能出现的那个 $\theta$。取 10 封里有 7 封垃圾邮件：$\theta = 0.7$ 时 $L = \binom{10}{7}\,0.7^{7}\,0.3^{3} = 0.267$；$\theta = 0.5$ 时只有 $0.117$。$L$ 对 $\theta$ 的曲线在 $0.7$ 处达到峰值；数据多十倍，峰值位置不变，但尖得多：数据越多，越确定。

alt.en: Likelihood of theta for 7 spam in 10 emails (blue) and 70 in 100 (orange), each scaled to peak 1. Both peak at theta 0.7; the larger sample is much narrower.
alt.zh: θ 的似然曲线：10 封里 7 封垃圾（蓝）和 100 封里 70 封（橙），各自缩放到峰值为 1。两者都在 θ=0.7 处最高，样本大的那条窄得多。

title.en: A likelihood is not a probability of $\theta$

body.en: $L(\theta)$ does not sum or integrate to 1 over $\theta$, and it does not say how probable it is that $\theta = 0.7$. It says how probable the *data* are if $\theta = 0.7$. To get a probability of $\theta$ you need a prior and Bayes' rule (MAP, below).
body.zh: $L(\theta)$ 对 $\theta$ 求和或积分并不等于 1，它也没说“$\theta = 0.7$ 有多可能”。它说的是：如果 $\theta = 0.7$，*数据*有多可能。要得到 $\theta$ 本身的概率，需要先验和贝叶斯公式（下面的 MAP）。

title.en: Deeper: MLE of a Bernoulli parameter, by calculus
title.zh: 深入：用微积分求伯努利参数的 MLE

say.en: Independent flips multiply. Each flip contributes the Bernoulli factor. Collecting exponents, $k = \sum_i x_i$ counts the heads. (The binomial coefficient would only add a constant that does not depend on $\theta$.)
say.zh: 独立的抛掷相乘。每次抛掷贡献一个伯努利因子。合并指数，$k = \sum_i x_i$ 是正面的次数。（二项系数只会多出一个与 $\theta$ 无关的常数。）

say.en: Take the log. It turns the product into a sum, which is easier to differentiate, and it avoids numbers like $10^{-300}$. Since $\log$ is increasing, $\ell$ and $L$ peak at the same $\theta$.
say.zh: 取对数。它把乘积变成和，更容易求导，也避免出现 $10^{-300}$ 这样的小数。因为 $\log$ 单调递增，$\ell$ 与 $L$ 在同一个 $\theta$ 处取最大。

say.en: Differentiate. The derivative of $\log(1-\theta)$ is $-1/(1-\theta)$ by the chain rule.
say.zh: 求导。$\log(1-\theta)$ 的导数按链式法则是 $-1/(1-\theta)$。

say.en: At the maximum the slope is zero. Move one term across: the 'pull' of the heads equals the 'pull' of the tails.
say.zh: 最大值处斜率为零。把一项移到另一边：正面的“拉力”等于反面的“拉力”。

say.en: Cross-multiply; the $k\theta$ terms cancel.
say.zh: 交叉相乘；$k\theta$ 项互相抵消。

say.en: The MLE is the **relative frequency** of heads: the fraction you observed.
say.zh: MLE 就是正面的**相对频率**：你观测到的那个比例。

say.en: The second derivative is negative everywhere, so $\ell$ is concave and this stationary point is the maximum, not a minimum.
say.zh: 二阶导数处处为负，所以 $\ell$ 是凹函数，这个驻点是最大值，不是最小值。

say.en: The curve of the previous page peaks exactly here.
say.zh: 上一页的曲线正好在这里达到峰值。

outro.en: So 'estimate the probability by the frequency' is not a rule of thumb: it is the maximiser of the likelihood.
outro.zh: 所以“用频率估计概率”不是经验法则，而是似然函数的最大点。

prompt.en: The MLE of the heads probability for 7 heads in 10 flips.
prompt.zh: 10 次抛掷 7 次正面时，正面概率的 MLE。

title.en: Deeper: MLE of a categorical distribution, with a Lagrange multiplier
title.zh: 深入：用拉格朗日乘子求类别分布的 MLE

say.en: A $K$-sided die rolled $N$ times, face $k$ seen $n_k$ times ($\sum_k n_k = N$). The likelihood is $\prod_k p_k^{n_k}$ (up to a constant counting factor); its log is this sum.
say.zh: 掷一个 $K$ 面骰子 $N$ 次，第 $k$ 面出现 $n_k$ 次（$\sum_k n_k = N$）。似然是 $\prod_k p_k^{n_k}$（差一个常数的计数因子）；取对数就是这个和。

say.en: The task is to maximise $\ell$ under the constraint. This time we cannot simply set derivatives to zero: without a constraint, $\ell$ grows by making every $p_k$ bigger. The probabilities must sum to 1.
say.zh: 任务是在约束下最大化 $\ell$。这次不能直接令导数为零：没有约束的话，把每个 $p_k$ 都变大，$\ell$ 就会增大。概率之和必须为 1。

say.en: The **Lagrangian** adds the constraint with a multiplier $\lambda$. At the constrained maximum, all partial derivatives of $\mathcal{L}$ vanish, and the derivative in $\lambda$ gives back the constraint itself.
say.zh: **拉格朗日函数**用乘子 $\lambda$ 把约束加进去。在带约束的最大值处，$\mathcal{L}$ 的所有偏导数都为零，对 $\lambda$ 的偏导数就是约束本身。

say.en: Differentiate with respect to one $p_k$: only its own term of the sums survives.
say.zh: 对某个 $p_k$ 求导：两个和里只剩它自己那一项。

say.en: Solve for $p_k$: every probability is proportional to its count; $\lambda$ is the common scale.
say.zh: 解出 $p_k$：每个概率都与它的计数成正比；$\lambda$ 是共同的比例。

say.en: Use the constraint to find the scale: the probabilities must add to 1, which fixes $\lambda$ at the total count.
say.zh: 用约束定出比例：概率之和必须为 1，由此 $\lambda$ 等于总次数。

say.en: Each face's MLE is its **relative frequency**. With $K=2$ this is the Bernoulli result of the last page. It is also what naive Bayes does when it estimates $P(\text{word} \mid \text{class})$ by counting.
say.zh: 每个面的 MLE 就是它的**相对频率**。$K=2$ 时就是上一页的伯努利结果。朴素贝叶斯用数数估计 $P(\text{词} \mid \text{类})$ 时做的也是这件事。

say.en: Twenty rolls of a six-sided die gave the counts 2, 3, 4, 3, 5, 3 for faces 1 to 6. The estimate for face 5.
say.zh: 六面骰子掷 20 次，点数 1 到 6 的次数是 2, 3, 4, 3, 5, 3。第 5 面的估计值。

outro.en: The multiplier $\lambda = N$ is the price of the constraint: how much the maximum of $\ell$ would rise per unit of extra probability mass allowed.
outro.zh: 乘子 $\lambda = N$ 是约束的“价格”：每多允许一个单位的概率质量，$\ell$ 的最大值能增加多少。

prompt.en: The MLE of the probability of face 5.

title.en: Where MLE goes wrong, and the nudge from a prior
title.zh: MLE 哪里不行，以及先验的“轻推”

text.en: MLE is one choice of estimator among many. Its weakness appears with little data. Suppose the only inbox we have contains no spam: $\hat\theta = 0/100 = 0$, so $P(\text{spam}) = 0$ and $P(\text{not spam}) = 1$: 'spam emails do not exist'. One empty sample does not justify such certainty.
text.zh: MLE 只是众多估计方法中的一种。数据少时它的弱点就暴露了。假设我们仅有的那个收件箱里没有垃圾邮件：$\hat\theta = 0/100 = 0$，于是 $P(\text{垃圾}) = 0$、$P(\text{非垃圾}) = 1$：“垃圾邮件不存在”。一个空样本撑不起这样的确定。

text.en: We usually do believe something beforehand (say, about 20 of 100 emails are spam). Treat $\theta$ itself as unknown with a **prior** $P(\theta)$ and apply Bayes' rule to get a **posterior** over $\theta$:
text.zh: 我们事先通常是有看法的（比如 100 封里大约 20 封是垃圾邮件）。把 $\theta$ 本身当成未知量，给它一个**先验** $P(\theta)$，再用贝叶斯公式得到 $\theta$ 的**后验**：

text.en: The **maximum a posteriori (MAP)** estimate is the peak of the posterior. For a Bernoulli parameter with a Beta$(a,b)$ prior it is $(a + k - 1)/(a + b + N - 2)$ (a standard result). A prior Beta$(21,81)$ encodes '20 spam in 100 imaginary emails'; with 0 spam in our 100 real ones: $(21+0-1)/(21+81+100-2) = 20/200 = 0.1$.
text.zh: **最大后验（MAP）**估计是后验的峰值。对带 Beta$(a,b)$ 先验的伯努利参数，它是 $(a + k - 1)/(a + b + N - 2)$（标准结果）。先验 Beta$(21,81)$ 相当于“100 封想象的邮件里有 20 封垃圾”；我们真实的 100 封里 0 封垃圾：$(21+0-1)/(21+81+100-2) = 20/200 = 0.1$。

text.en: The estimate moved from $0$ to $0.1$, halfway between the data (0) and the belief (0.2), because we had as much real as imaginary data. With 10,000 real emails the prior would barely count.
text.zh: 估计从 $0$ 移到了 $0.1$，正好在数据（0）和看法（0.2）的中间，因为真实数据和想象数据一样多。真实邮件有 10000 封时，先验就几乎不起作用了。

text.en: Read the prior as **pseudo-counts**: imaginary observations added to the real ones. You will meet this again as Laplace smoothing in naive Bayes. MLE is MAP with a flat prior.
text.zh: 把先验读成**伪计数**：加在真实观测之上的想象观测。你会在朴素贝叶斯里再次遇到它，名字是拉普拉斯平滑。MLE 就是先验平坦时的 MAP。

summary.en: MLE of a Gaussian, in four lines

text.en: Data $x_1,\dots,x_N$ independent from $\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$. Log-likelihood:
text.zh: 数据 $x_1,\dots,x_N$ 独立取自 $\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$。对数似然：

text.en: Setting $\partial\ell/\partial\sigma = 0$ in the same way gives $\hat\sigma^2 = \frac1N\sum_i (x_i-\hat\mu)^2$. The MLE of the mean is the sample mean; the MLE of the variance divides by $N$, not $N-1$ (it is slightly biased low). This is also why least squares and the Gaussian are tied together in linear regression.
text.zh: 用同样的办法令 $\partial\ell/\partial\sigma = 0$，得 $\hat\sigma^2 = \frac1N\sum_i (x_i-\hat\mu)^2$。均值的 MLE 是样本均值；方差的 MLE 除以 $N$ 而不是 $N-1$（略微偏小）。线性回归里最小二乘与高斯噪声的联系也由此而来。

say.en: How surprised are you when $x$ happens? Not at all if $P(x)=1$ (0 bits); a little for a likely event; a lot for a rare one. $-\log_2 P(x)$ measures it in **bits**: a fair coin landing heads is 1 bit, a 1-in-1024 event is 10 bits.
say.zh: $x$ 发生时你有多惊讶？$P(x)=1$ 时毫不惊讶（0 比特）；常见事件只有一点点；罕见事件非常惊讶。$-\log_2 P(x)$ 用**比特**来度量：公平硬币出现正面是 1 比特，千分之一的事件是 10 比特。

say.en: Why a logarithm? Two independent events: probabilities multiply, and we want surprises to add. The log turns products into sums, and it is the only sensible measure with this property.
say.zh: 为什么是对数？两个独立事件：概率相乘，而我们希望惊讶程度相加。对数把乘积变成和，满足这个性质的合理度量只有它。

say.en: **Entropy** is the average surprise of the variable, the expectation of $s(X)$: surprise of each outcome weighted by how often it occurs. High entropy = unpredictable, low entropy = predictable.
say.zh: **熵**是这个变量的平均惊讶，即 $s(X)$ 的期望：每个结果的惊讶按它出现的频率加权。熵高 = 难以预测，熵低 = 容易预测。

say.en: A fair coin: each outcome is 1 bit and they are equally likely.
say.zh: 公平硬币：每个结果是 1 比特，且概率相等。

say.en: A biased coin: the common outcome (0.15 bits) is rarely a surprise, the rare one (3.32 bits) is a big one but seldom happens. The average is far below 1.
say.zh: 一枚偏心硬币：常见的结果（0.15 比特）几乎不让人惊讶，罕见的结果（3.32 比特）很惊讶但很少发生。平均值远低于 1。

say.en: Uniform over $K$ outcomes has entropy $\log_2 K$, the maximum possible for $K$ outcomes: nothing is more predictable than anything else. A fair die: $\log_2 6 = 2.585$. A certain outcome: $H = 0$ (with $0\log 0 := 0$).
say.zh: $K$ 个结果均匀分布的熵是 $\log_2 K$，是 $K$ 个结果能达到的最大值：没有哪个结果比别的更好预测。公平骰子：$\log_2 6 = 2.585$。确定的结果：$H = 0$（约定 $0\log 0 := 0$）。

intro.en: The deck stops at probability, but the next lectures need one more idea from it, and it comes straight from expectation.
intro.zh: 讲义讲到概率为止，但后面几讲还需要从中再引出一个想法，它直接来自期望。

outro.en: **The bridge to decision trees:** a good question to ask about an instance is one whose answer removes the most surprise about its label. Information gain is the entropy of the label before the question minus its average entropy after. Also: the MLE of a categorical distribution is exactly the distribution that minimises the cross-entropy to the observed frequencies, which is the loss of logistic regression later.
outro.zh: **通向决策树的桥：**对一个实例最值得问的问题，是答案能消除关于标签的最多惊讶的那个。信息增益就是提问前标签的熵，减去提问后的平均熵。另外：类别分布的 MLE，恰好就是与观测频率的交叉熵最小的那个分布，而交叉熵正是后面逻辑回归的损失。

title.en: A test for a rare disease

prompt.en: 2% of a population has a disease. A test is positive for 90% of those who have it, and also for 8% of those who do not. A person tests positive. What is the probability they have the disease? (3 decimals)
prompt.zh: 人群中 2% 患有某种疾病。检测对患者 90% 呈阳性，对非患者也有 8% 呈阳性。某人检测呈阳性。他患病的概率是多少？（三位小数）

explain.en: Bayes with the evidence expanded: $\frac{0.02 \times 0.9}{0.02 \times 0.9 + 0.98 \times 0.08} = \frac{0.018}{0.018 + 0.0784} = 0.187$. Check with 10,000 people: 200 ill, 180 of them positive; 9,800 healthy, 784 positive; $180/(180+784)$.

hints.en: Prior 0.02, likelihood 0.9; the evidence adds the false positives.
hints.zh: 先验 0.02，似然 0.9；证据项要加上假阳性。

label.en: $P(A \mid B) = P(B \mid A)$ whenever $A$ and $B$ are both possible
label.zh: 只要 $A$ 与 $B$ 都可能发生，就有 $P(A \mid B) = P(B \mid A)$

feedback.en: They are equal only if $P(A) = P(B)$. $P(\text{heart} \mid \text{red}) = 1/2$ but $P(\text{red} \mid \text{heart}) = 1$.
feedback.zh: 只有 $P(A) = P(B)$ 时才相等。$P(\text{红桃} \mid \text{红色}) = 1/2$，而 $P(\text{红色} \mid \text{红桃}) = 1$。

feedback.en: The evidence term is missing: divide by $P(B)$, or the result need not sum to 1.
feedback.zh: 漏了证据项：要除以 $P(B)$，否则结果的总和不一定是 1。

feedback.en: That is the independence formula for the joint $P(A,B)$, not a conditional.
feedback.zh: 那是联合概率 $P(A,B)$ 的独立性公式，不是条件概率。

explain.en: Both product rules give $P(A,B)$; dividing by $P(B)$ leaves Bayes' rule.
explain.zh: 两种乘法规则都给出 $P(A,B)$；除以 $P(B)$ 就得到贝叶斯公式。

prompt.en: Write down Bayes' rule, name each of its four parts, and say in one line why it is useful for classification. (Section A style.)
prompt.zh: 写出贝叶斯公式，说出它四个部分的名称，并用一句话说明它为什么对分类有用。（A 部分风格。）

key_points.zh: 后验、似然、先验、证据（归一化常数）

key_points.en: P(B) = sum over a of P(B|a)P(a)
Lets us get P(class | features) from P(features | class) and the class prior
key_points.zh: 让我们由 P(特征|类别) 和类别先验得到 P(类别|特征)

model_answer.en: P(A|B) = P(B|A) P(A) / P(B). Here P(A|B) is the posterior (belief in hypothesis A after seeing evidence B), P(B|A) the likelihood (how probable the evidence is if A is true), P(A) the prior (belief before the evidence) and P(B) the evidence, a normalising constant equal to the sum over all hypotheses a of P(B|a)P(a). In classification it lets us compute P(class | features), which we want, from P(features | class), which is easy to estimate from training data, and the class prior.
model_answer.zh: P(A|B) = P(B|A) P(A) / P(B). Here P(A|B) is the posterior (belief in hypothesis A after seeing evidence B), P(B|A) the likelihood (how probable the evidence is if A is true), P(A) the prior (belief before the evidence) and P(B) the evidence, a normalising constant equal to the sum over all hypotheses a of P(B|a)P(a). In classification it lets us compute P(class | features), which we want, from P(features | class), which is easy to estimate from training data, and the class prior.

explain.en: Formula, four names, and the purpose. Each is a mark.
explain.zh: 公式、四个名称、用途，每项一分。

title.zh: 最大似然：是什么、怎么求、弱点

prompt.en: Explain maximum likelihood estimation for the probability of heads of a coin, from 7 heads in 10 tosses. Say what is maximised, why we take the log, what the answer is, and one weakness. (Section A/B style, 4-6 lines.)
prompt.zh: 以 10 次抛硬币 7 次正面为例，解释对正面概率的最大似然估计。说明最大化的是什么、为什么取对数、答案是多少，以及一个弱点。（A/B 部分风格，4-6 行。）

key_points.en: Maximise the likelihood of the data, P(data; theta) = theta^7 (1-theta)^3
key_points.zh: 最大化数据的似然 P(data; θ) = θ^7 (1-θ)^3

key_points.en: Log turns the product into a sum, easier derivative, same maximiser, avoids underflow
key_points.zh: 取对数把乘积变成和，求导更容易，最大点不变，避免下溢

key_points.en: Derivative zero gives theta = k/N = 0.7 (relative frequency)
key_points.zh: 导数为零得 θ = k/N = 0.7（相对频率）

key_points.en: Weakness: little data gives extreme estimates (0 heads gives 0); fix with a prior (MAP)
key_points.zh: 弱点：数据少时估计极端（0 次正面得 0）；用先验（MAP）修正

model_answer.en: MLE chooses the parameter theta that makes the observed data most probable, i.e. it maximises the likelihood L(theta) = theta^7 (1-theta)^3. We maximise the log-likelihood 7 log theta + 3 log(1-theta) instead: the log turns the product into a sum, is easier to differentiate, has the same maximiser because log is increasing, and avoids numerical underflow. Setting the derivative 7/theta - 3/(1-theta) to zero gives theta = 7/10 = 0.7, the relative frequency. A weakness: with little data the estimate can be extreme, for example 0 heads in 5 tosses gives theta = 0, claiming tails is certain; a prior and MAP estimation (or smoothing) corrects this.
model_answer.zh: MLE chooses the parameter theta that makes the observed data most probable, i.e. it maximises the likelihood L(theta) = theta^7 (1-theta)^3. We maximise the log-likelihood 7 log theta + 3 log(1-theta) instead: the log turns the product into a sum, is easier to differentiate, has the same maximiser because log is increasing, and avoids numerical underflow. Setting the derivative 7/theta - 3/(1-theta) to zero gives theta = 7/10 = 0.7, the relative frequency. A weakness: with little data the estimate can be extreme, for example 0 heads in 5 tosses gives theta = 0, claiming tails is certain; a prior and MAP estimation (or smoothing) corrects this.

explain.en: Four marks: what is maximised, why log, the answer, a weakness.
explain.zh: 四分：最大化什么、为什么取对数、答案、弱点。

rows.en: $P(A,B) = P(A\mid B)P(B)$; $P(A_1..A_n) = \prod_i P(A_i\mid A_{<i})$, any order, no assumption
rows.zh: $P(A,B) = P(A\mid B)P(B)$；$P(A_1..A_n) = \prod_i P(A_i\mid A_{<i})$，任意顺序，无需假设

rows.en: $P(A,B) = P(A)P(B)$; conditional: given $C$; neither implies the other; disjoint $\ne$ independent
rows.zh: $P(A,B) = P(A)P(B)$；条件独立：给定 $C$；互不蕴含；互斥 $\ne$ 独立

rows.en: posterior = likelihood $\times$ prior / evidence; beware the base rate
rows.zh: 后验 = 似然 $\times$ 先验 / 证据；当心基础概率

rows.en: Bernoulli $p^x(1-p)^{1-x}$; binomial $\binom{N}{x}p^x(1-p)^{N-x}$; multinomial $\frac{N!}{\prod x_k!}\prod p_k^{x_k}$; Gaussian $\mu,\sigma$
rows.zh: 伯努利 $p^x(1-p)^{1-x}$；二项 $\binom{N}{x}p^x(1-p)^{N-x}$；多项 $\frac{N!}{\prod x_k!}\prod p_k^{x_k}$；高斯 $\mu,\sigma$

rows.en: maximise $\log L$; Bernoulli $k/N$; categorical $n_k/N$ (Lagrange); fails with little data
rows.zh: 最大化 $\log L$；伯努利 $k/N$；类别 $n_k/N$（拉格朗日）；数据少时不可靠
后验 $\propto$ 先验 $\times$ 似然；先验 = 伪计数

rows.zh: $-\sum P\log_2 P$ = 期望的惊讶；均匀时最大 $\log_2 K$；确定时为 0
